topics.title: Welcome
topics.step:
This plugin tidies the folder tree Penumbra shows you. It never edits, renames or deletes your mod files, and it never changes what a mod does in game.

This walkthrough is seven short steps. You can leave at any time - it will not come back.

topics.title: Step 1: Scan
topics.step:
Open the Scan tab and press Refresh mod list.

That reads your library from Penumbra and works out what kind of mod each one is. Nothing else in the plugin updates on its own, so this comes first, and again whenever you install or remove mods.

topics.title: Step 2: Protect anything that must not move
topics.step:
On the Protect tab, tick any mod or folder that should keep exactly where it is. Protected items are skipped by every sort and by Apply.

Heliosphere-managed mods are protected for you automatically, because Heliosphere owns where they live.

topics.title: Step 3: Choose a layout
topics.step:
On the Sort tab, pick a grouping from Group by, decide whether gear and NPC mods get subfolders, and press Sort.

Nothing moves yet. Sort only works out where each mod would go.

topics.title: Step 4: Check the plan
topics.step:
The Review Changes tab shows every mod's current folder beside the proposed one.

Anything that would block the move is listed at the top in red. Two mods landing on the same path is the usual one, and Protect & Skip All Blocking Mods clears them in one go.

topics.title: Step 5: Apply
topics.step:
When the plan looks right, press Apply on the Review Changes tab. That is the only step in this loop that changes your library.

A backup is taken automatically first, and the History tab can put everything back. Nothing you have done before this point touched anything.

topics.title: That is the whole loop
topics.step:
Scan, protect, sort, review, apply.

Every control has an explanation if you hover it, and the Help tab holds all of them at greater length along with a link to the full guide. You can reopen this walkthrough from there.

topics.title: Penumbra is not responding
topics.step:
This plugin reads everything through Penumbra, and Penumbra does not appear to be loaded right now.

Enable Penumbra, then reopen this window and the walkthrough will start properly. Nothing here will work until then, so there is no point walking you through it now.

topics.title: What this plugin does
topics.body:
It proposes a tidy folder layout for your Penumbra mod list, shows you the whole plan, and only changes anything when you press Apply.

It organises the folder tree Penumbra shows you. It never edits, renames, moves or deletes the mod files themselves on disk, and it never changes what a mod does in game.

The usual order is: Scan to read your library, Protect anything that must not move, Sort to propose a layout, Review Changes to check it, then Apply.

topics.title: What is safe, and what is not
topics.body:
Everything that can change your library is on this list: Apply, Restore, Clean Up Selected Folders, Rollback Folder Cleanup, and the recovery panel's Continue and Restore Previous State. Everything else - scanning, sorting, searching, exporting - is read-only, no matter how it looks.

Sorting never moves anything. It fills in a proposed path for each mod, which you can look over on Review Changes and discard by simply sorting differently.

A backup snapshot is taken automatically before every Apply and every Restore, so there is always a way back. The History tab lists them.

Protected mods are excluded from every sort and from Apply. Restore is the one exception, and it says so: it reproduces a snapshot exactly, including for mods that are currently protected.

topics.title: Scan
topics.body:
Reads every mod from Penumbra and works out what kind of mod each one is. Nothing else in the plugin updates on its own, so run this first, and again whenever you install, remove or move mods outside the plugin.

The scan runs in the background and the game stays responsive. If your mod list changes while it is running, the results are discarded rather than shown, because they no longer describe your library.

topics.title: Protect
topics.body:
Marks mods that must keep their current folder. A protected mod is skipped by every sort and by Apply.

Protection comes from three places: the mod's own checkbox, any protected folder above it, and Heliosphere. The note beside a mod says which one applies. Only the first is a per-mod choice you make here.

topics.title: Sort
topics.body:
Chooses the folder layout to propose. Pick a grouping, decide whether gear and NPC mods get subfolders, and press Sort.

Nothing moves. Sort only fills in proposed paths, which you then check on Review Changes.

The bottom of the tab is manual assignment, for putting specific mods somewhere by hand instead of by rule.

topics.title: Review Changes
topics.body:
Shows every mod's current folder beside its proposed one, along with anything that would block Apply.

Errors are listed at the top and must be cleared before Apply is available. A collision means two mods would end up at the same path; a protected-mod error means something tried to move a mod you protected.

This tab also holds folder cleanup, which removes empty folder entries left behind in Penumbra's own folder file. That is separate from moving mods and has its own backup.

topics.title: History
topics.body:
Every backup snapshot, newest first. A snapshot records where each mod was at that moment.

Backups are taken automatically before each Apply and Restore, and you can take one yourself at any time with an optional label.

Restore is exact: it reproduces the snapshot's paths even for mods that are currently protected or Heliosphere-managed. That is deliberate, and it is the one place protection does not apply.

topics.title: Search
topics.body:
Looks up which mod changes a given item. Entirely read-only.

Build the index first, then filter by mod name, by item name, by category, and by equipment slot for gear.

Since Penumbra 1.7 its own Mods tab has a native search syntax that covers much of this, so this tab may be retired later.

topics.title: If something went wrong
topics.body:
If an Apply or Restore is interrupted - a crash, a force-quit, the game closing mid-operation - the plugin notices on the next start and shows a recovery panel above the tabs. Nothing else can run until you resolve it.

You get three choices: accept the current state and move on, finish what was interrupted, or roll back to how things were before it started. The panel says which are available; a greyed-out option means the plugin no longer has the file it would need.

If several operations were interrupted, they are resolved one at a time, and the per-operation buttons permanently abandon that one operation rather than repairing it.

For anything else, Create Diagnostic Dump on Review Changes writes a file describing the plugin's state, which is the most useful thing to attach to a bug report.

topics.title: Where your files are
topics.body:
This plugin keeps its own settings, backups and exports in its Dalamud config folder. Show Config File on Review Changes opens it.

The folder tree you see in Penumbra lives in Penumbra's own organization.json, not here. Folder cleanup is the only feature that writes to it, and it takes a backup first.

Your actual mod files are never touched by this plugin, wherever Penumbra keeps them.

topics.title: Refresh mod list
topics.short: Re-reads every mod from Penumbra and re-classifies it. Nothing moves. Run it after installing, removing or moving mods elsewhere - nothing here updates on its own.

topics.title: Live events
topics.short: Penumbra events as they happen. Informational only: seeing a mod appear here does not re-scan, so run Refresh mod list yourself afterwards.

topics.title: Toggle protect all
topics.short: Protects every mod if any are unprotected, and unprotects them all otherwise. A protected mod keeps its current folder through every Sort and Apply.

topics.title: Toggle Heliosphere protection
topics.short: Protects or unprotects every Heliosphere-managed mod at once. Unprotecting lasts this session only - the next Scan re-protects them, since Heliosphere owns where they live.

topics.title: Protected folders
topics.short: Protecting a folder protects everything under it at any depth, including mods that land there later. Checking Gear also covers Gear/Feet and everything below it.

topics.title: Protected mods
topics.short: Protects one mod wherever it sits. A mod can also be protected by its folder or by Heliosphere - the note beside it says which, and those have no checkbox here.

topics.title: Protected by Heliosphere
topics.short: Protected because Heliosphere manages it, not by its own checkbox. Heliosphere owns where it lives, so the plugin never proposes moving it during Sort or Apply.

topics.title: Group by
topics.short: Chooses the folder structure proposed for every unprotected mod. Nothing moves until you press Apply on the Review Changes tab.

topics.title: Split gear by equipment slot
topics.short: Puts gear mods in Gear/Feet, Gear/Head and so on instead of a single Gear folder. Mods whose slot could not be identified stay in Gear.

topics.title: Split NPC mods by kind
topics.short: Puts NPC mods in NPC/NPCs, NPC/Bosses or NPC/Enemies. Turn it off to keep every NPC mod in one NPC folder.

topics.title: Sort
topics.short: Works out a new folder for every unprotected mod and shows it on the Review Changes tab. Your library is not touched until you apply it.

topics.title: Also use the NPC list scraped from the wiki
topics.short: Recognises far more character names, at the cost of matching some very common words. Turned off in this version while we confirm it is safe.

topics.title: Import Workbook
topics.short: Reads folder choices back from an exported spreadsheet, so you can plan a large reorganisation outside the game.

topics.title: Assign selected mods
topics.short: Sets the proposed folder for every checked mod. Unlike Sort, this does not renumber name clashes - it reports them as errors on Review Changes instead.

topics.title: Refresh NPC list from wiki
topics.short: Rebuilds the opt-in scraped NPC list from the wiki. The curated list bundled with the plugin is separate and never needs refreshing.

topics.title: Apply
topics.short: Moves every unprotected mod whose proposed folder differs from its current one. This is the only control on this tab that changes your library, and a backup snapshot is taken first, automatically.

topics.title: Export
topics.short: Writes the proposed changes to a text file you can read outside the game. Your library is not touched.

topics.title: Show Config File
topics.short: Opens the folder holding this plugin's own settings and data files. Changes nothing.

topics.title: Create Diagnostic Dump
topics.short: Writes a text file describing the plugin's current state, for troubleshooting or a bug report. Your library is not touched.

topics.title: Workbook destinations
topics.short: Which folder layout the exported spreadsheet should suggest. This affects only the exported file, not the proposed paths shown above.

topics.title: Export Workbook
topics.short: Writes every mod and its destination to a spreadsheet you can edit outside the game, then bring back with Import Workbook on the Sort tab.

topics.title: Protect & Skip All Blocking Mods
topics.short: Protects every mod named in the errors above so it stops blocking Apply. Those mods keep their current folder instead of moving.

topics.title: Re-read organization.json
topics.short: Re-reads Penumbra's folder file from disk to refresh the list below. If Penumbra has not written a change out yet, re-reading will not reveal it.

topics.title: Clean Up Selected Folders
topics.short: Removes the checked empty folder entries from Penumbra's folder file. No mod is touched. Run Rediscover Mods in Penumbra afterwards.

topics.title: Rollback Folder Cleanup
topics.short: Restores Penumbra's folder file from the backup taken before the last cleanup, undoing that cleanup only. No mod is moved.

topics.title: Create Backup
topics.short: Saves every mod's current folder as a snapshot you can return to later. Backups are also taken automatically before every Apply and Restore.

topics.title: Restore
topics.short: Moves every mod back to the folder it had in this snapshot. Exact: it moves protected and Heliosphere mods too, which Sort and Apply never do.

topics.title: Delete snapshot
topics.short: Deletes this backup permanently. Your mods are not touched - only the saved snapshot goes, and it cannot be recovered afterwards.

topics.title: Build/Refresh Index
topics.short: Reads every mod's changed items from Penumbra and builds the searchable index below. Read-only: it never moves, protects or alters a mod.

topics.title: Mod name contains
topics.short: Shows only mods whose name contains this text. It combines with the item filter and the category boxes - a mod has to satisfy all of them.

topics.title: Item contains
topics.short: Shows only mods that change an item whose name contains this text, such as one specific piece of gear.

topics.title: Categories
topics.short: Limits results to these mod categories. Unknown covers mods whose changed items the plugin could not classify.

topics.title: Slots
topics.short: Limits Gear results to these equipment slots. Unresolved covers gear whose slot could not be pinned to a single unambiguous match.

topics.title: Keep Current State
topics.short: Accepts whatever Penumbra has now as correct and unblocks the plugin. Nothing is moved or undone - the interrupted operation is simply closed.

topics.title: Continue
topics.short: Finishes the interrupted operation from where it stopped, moving the mods it had not reached yet.

topics.title: Restore Previous State
topics.short: Moves every mod back to where it was before the interrupted operation started, undoing the part of it that did complete.

topics.title: Keep Current State (one operation)
topics.short: Permanently abandons this one operation - it can never be continued or rolled back. The rest stay blocked, and one of them may then become resolvable on its own.

topics.title: Accept Current State and Close All Interrupted Operations
topics.short: Permanently abandons every interrupted operation at once. None can be continued or rolled back. No mod moves - it only stops the plugin blocking further actions.

topics.title: Export my layout as a template
topics.short: Builds a shareable template from the folders your mods are in now, not from pending proposals. A review screen opens first, because a template lists your mod names.

topics.title: Template name
topics.short: How your template appears in someone else's list. Required. The file on disk gets a tidied version of it, but this is the name other people see.

topics.title: Fallback grouping
topics.short: Where an importer's mods go when your template does not mention them. Same groupings the Sort tab offers, so a template can only ask for a layout this plugin can produce.

topics.title: Folders
topics.short: Every folder that goes into the template, empty ones included, so an importer gets your whole structure. Unticking a folder also leaves out the mods inside it.

topics.title: Search mods
topics.short: Narrows the list you are looking at. It never changes what is included - Include all and Exclude all always apply to every mod, not just the ones shown.

topics.title: Save to templates folder
topics.short: Writes the template as a .json file you can send to anyone. Use this for a real library: it works at any size, unlike a share code.

topics.title: Copy share code
topics.short: Copies the template as one line of text to paste into chat. Small templates only - a chat message holds about 2000 characters and a big library will not fit.

topics.title: Templates
topics.body:
A template is a folder layout someone shared. Importing one proposes where your mods would go; mods you both have land where they put them, and the rest follow the fallback grouping they chose.

Nothing is applied until you review it on Review Changes.

Export builds a template from your own library. It shows you every mod name that would be included first, because whoever you send it to can read that list.

topics.title: Refresh list
topics.short: Re-reads the templates folder. Use it after dropping a .json in there yourself. Files that are not readable templates are listed as skipped rather than hidden.

topics.title: Open templates folder
topics.short: Opens the folder templates are kept in, creating it if it does not exist yet. Handy for putting a file there by hand, or for finding one you saved to send to someone.

topics.title: Import template file
topics.short: Copies a .json someone shared into your templates folder. It is checked before it is stored, and it never overwrites a template you already have - a name clash gets a numbered filename.

topics.title: Preview against my library
topics.short: Works out where this template would put your mods and shows the folder tree with counts, plus how many of your mods it matched. Nothing is staged or moved yet.

topics.title: Apply this template to my proposals
topics.short: Fills in proposed paths from the preview. Still nothing moves - open Review Changes to check them and apply from there, exactly as with any sort.
